design: Owner decision 2026-10-03: six formalization paths of strongly different strategy, each a routed question TREE (5-10 questions along a root-to-leaf path) with its own deterministic heuristics into SOP Lang; harness tools/eval/six-paths/, questions as data in config/knowledge/formalizer-six-paths-v1 (research layer, chat false). Results: experiments/proposal/six-paths-results.md.

paths.A_method: top-down templates: asked parts -> goal type (closed menu, filtered by structure) -> method of config/knowledge/formalizer-methods-v1 -> slots by registry index or sub-goal (depth <= 3); SOP from the method templates (method-library machine, primitives calculate/rank/deduce).
paths.B_compute: bottom-up program: asked parts -> `name = expression` lines over v1..vn with 2 verified F1 exemplars (section leave-one-out) -> one re-ask only on a static-analysis violation; SOP by lowering the AST (lib/formalize/expression-program.mjs, wrapped, never edited).
paths.C_equations: Polya: unknowns -> data with roles -> conditions as equations/inequalities -> what is asked (value, largest, smallest, check, possible) -> on no or several solutions one question for the corrected conditions; solved by deterministic algebra (propagation, bound isolation) into session rules, residual integer systems by the constraint wire.
paths.D_backward: goal regression: goals -> for each quantity its inputs (registry numbers, plan quantities, new intermediates) and a closed combination menu -> recursion to registry data; SOP as a rule graph.
paths.E_controlled_english: the model rewrites facts and question into a fixed set of sentence patterns; a deterministic parser compiles them (arithmetic to session rules, unary logic to the deduce primitive); rejected sentences are named in one re-ask.
paths.F_analogy: retrieve verified solved computations (F1 index plus the experiment's own verified pool), never the same problem, the same section or a content-word duplicate; choose one, map its inputs by index, confirm; SOP is the verified computation with substituted values.

hypothesis: H1: the six paths have weakly correlated errors (pairwise wrong-together and agreeing-wrongly rates well below the product of their error rates would suggest for one shared strategy), so 'two paths of different strategy agree on the executed result on the problem's numbers and on 3 perturbations' verifies a formalization with precision >= 95% at a coverage that grows with each dev iteration. H2: at least two paths reach >= 40% correct alone on tier small.
model: tier small of LLMAPIProvider (openference Qwen3.8 27b), thinking off, temperature 0, purpose job:six-paths, run header per run, x-llmapiprovider-no-fallback: 1 (no answer from another model), the proxy response cache on. No other model judges.
judge: The book answers (datasets_sources/books/eval/items.jsonl, local only; never copied into git; sealed suites never read). Deterministic verdict with format normalization (tools/eval/six-paths/score.mjs: tolerance, the gold's rounding, percent/fraction, unit conversion from the memory's unit facts, clock time, multi-part gold, yes/no in the gold text, name sets); a format-only match is counted correct and listed apart; a remaining text answer gets one cached compare-only call on tier small; structural gold defects are counted apart. The controlling agent reviews wrong and no-result traces itself to fix questions and heuristics (generic fixes only).
sample: Scorable book problems (number, yes/no, names, lists of numbers or names; explanations excluded), stratified by book (7 books, round robin), seeded hash order; every draw excludes every id of an earlier six-paths run.

procedure.dev_iteration: 20 fresh problems, all six paths on each (per-path quality and error correlation measurable). After each iteration: fix the worst path's questions or heuristics (generic only), then draw a fresh 20.
procedure.measurement: Every 3-4 dev iterations: 100 fresh problems; the two strongest paths first, the other paths only when those two do not agree.
procedure.verification: Executed results compared on the original numbers and on 3 seeded perturbations of every distinct registry number (lib/formalize/dual-check.mjs perturbations); never syntactically. 'Verified' = the largest cluster of pairwise-agreeing paths has >= 2 members and is strictly larger than the next cluster.

stopping.bad_path_rule: A path that stays below 15% correct alone after 2 dev iterations AND adds no unique correct answer (no problem where it alone is correct) is redesigned once or dropped; a redesigned path that is again below 15% with no unique correct answer after 1 more iteration is dropped.
stopping.harness_break: If more than 20% of a path's runs in an iteration end in an infrastructure failure (proxy errors, engine errors) the iteration is repaired and rerun from the cache, not counted.
stopping.budget: At most 400 plan credits for the whole experiment (0.1 per small call); at most one rerun per question set; stop the dev loop when two consecutive iterations change no path's correct rate by more than 2 problems and verified precision is stable.
stopping.early_stop: A measurement stage stops after the first 100 if the verified precision interval (Wilson 95%) is decisive (lower bound >= 90% or upper bound < 90%).

metrics: Per path: correct alone, wrong, no result, gold defect, format-only, mean and maximum questions, seconds per problem; pairwise wrong-together and agreeing-wrongly tables; verified coverage and precision for 2 of N agree; unique correct answers per path; no-result reasons; model calls and cache hits.
deviations: 2026-10-03 (coordinator, owner idea): a second arm runs the same paths on tier tiny on the same ids (dev1), purpose job:six-paths-tiny, no fallback.

2026-10-03 (owner decision): design changed to TINY FIRST. Batches of 100 fresh problems stratified by book run all paths on tiny (local, free, up to 32 in flight, one process); tier small runs only on the residue (problems where no tiny 2-of-N agreement verified a correct answer). Analysis and question changes happen only between batches. The dev-iteration/measurement split of the original procedure is replaced by these batches; the bad-path rule applies per batch on tiny (a path below 15% on tiny with no unique correct answer after 2 batches is redesigned once or dropped).

2026-10-03: dev1 path A was broken by a harness defect (String.prototype.sub made every slot a sub-goal); A was rerun on dev1 with the fix from the proxy cache plus new calls for the changed questions (harness_break rule).

2026-10-03 (owner requirement): the judge normalizes formats before scoring (tolerance, rounding, percent/fraction, units from memory unit facts, clock, multi-part gold, yes/no in text, name sets); one cached compare-only call on small for remaining name answers; structural gold defects (numeric gold incidental to a text answer) are excluded from sampling and from precision.
2026-10-03 (batch2 finding): a constant yes/no profile (no number moves it) needs 3 agreeing paths instead of 2; all batches rescored with this rule.

2026-10-03 (owner decision): batches replaced by SEQUENTIAL ROUNDS: problems drawn one at a time (books round robin across rounds), tiny first (paths A,B,C,D,E), small on the residue (B,C,A); FAILURE = no verified correct answer after the small pass; a round stops at its 5th failure; progress metric = run length per round and the cumulative solved/attempted ratio; between rounds: deep analysis of the 5 failures, generic fixes, regression of every solved problem (zero losses), report every ~5 rounds.

2026-10-03 (pruning rule): F parked after batch1/batch2 (no correct answer on tiny, no unique answer) until the verified index has several hundred entries; its pool now admits gold-verified programs. E and D redesigned once (batch2) and kept until a verdict in the first rounds.

2026-10-03 (owner clarification): rounds measure tiny only; small is diagnostic on failures and never counts as solved; the run-length curve is reported under both rules. Path Z (tiny's direct answer, FINAL ANSWER line) added with acceptance (a) Z + one symbolic path, (b) two symbolic paths. Symbolic answer equivalence (lib/formalize/equivalence.mjs) decides comparisons; the equivalence model tier is not used (false positives in calibration).
status: stopped by the owner 2026-10-03 after 4 sequential rounds (tiny-only run length 5, 8, 5, 5): see experiments/proposal/six-paths-results.md
